title: Run Lucas Gate before the Jev decision evaluation
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run Lucas Gate before the Jev decision evaluation**

This driver calls `policy.evaluate_decision` before `run_typed_track`, as do the other gate drivers added here. That reverses the explicit `AGENTS.md` lane requirement, “Lucas Gate v2 first, Jev for decisions/dispositions,” so these receipts do not demonstrate the required gate sequence. Move the Lucas assessment ahead of the Jev call in the drivers and distinguish the historical receipts from evidence produced under the corrected sequence.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L122-L122](https://github.com/Treystu/harness/blob/f0957d647e60b017ef792b5718cb016a0b277441/AGENTS.md#L122-L122)

All 32 `gates_*.py` drivers in that lane keep the same order (for example `gates_624.py` jev=48 lucas=64, `gates_406`-era `gates_482.py` jev=47 lucas=63), so the AGENTS.md sequence is still reversed.

pr_title: evidence(sergeant): gate receipts for turns 2026-11-19 (cars 2-5 + CANON-1)
title: Read the decision signals using their returned field names
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the decision signals using their returned field names**

`evaluate_decision` returns the composed fields `disposition_lead`, `advances_goal` and `is_destructive` (see `harness/jev_packs.py::compose_decision_verdict`), not `lead`, `advanced` and `destructive`. These lookups therefore silently discard all three signals, which is visible as three null values in `gates-620.json` and the other new receipts. Use the actual returned keys when serializing and printing the signals; otherwise reviewers cannot inspect the probabilities and lead underlying the recorded investigate/escalate decisions without finding the separate ledger.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: evidence/lane-sessions/sergeant-2026-11-19/gates_620.py:77-79 serializes `verdict.get("lead")`, `verdict.get("advanced")`, `verdict.get("destructive")`, but `harness/jev_packs.py:2641-2652` (returned verbatim by `harness/jev_policy.py:1730-1732`) composes `disposition_lead`, `advances_goal` and `is_destructive`. `evidence/lane-sessions/sergeant-2026-11-19/gates-620.json` records all three as null under `product_jev`.

pr_title: #475: record per-attempt http_status and timestamps for panel and Jev calls
title: Preserve wire attempts across chat-level retries
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve wire attempts across chat-level retries**

When a panel or judge call retries after a reasoning-parameter rejection, `chat.py` invokes `transport.post()` twice inside one `chat_routed()` call. Resetting the collection on every POST discards the first request's attempts before the panel can consume them, so a real `[400, 200]` sequence is persisted as `[200]`, understating attempts and hiding recovered calls. The same problem affects the affordable-budget retry. Initialize the collection at the logical call boundary and preserve it across the constituent POSTs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: The mutable per-transport wire collection the finding names no longer exists: `harness/_http.py:417-421` emits one `provider_http_attempt` event per wire attempt with `request_id` and a per-POST `wire_attempt` counter, and `:460-462`/`:484-486` emit each response status as its own event. A second `transport.post()` from a chat-level retry therefore adds its own attempt events instead of resetting a collection, so a real [400, 200] sequence reaches the stream as both attempts; `harness/_http.py` no longer defines any `_WIRE` accumulator (`git grep` for `_WIRE` at 8fc28a0e matches nothing).

pr_title: #475: record per-attempt http_status and timestamps for panel and Jev calls
title: Isolate the strict Jev call from previous wire traces
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate the strict Jev call from previous wire traces**

When a strict Jev assessment follows an ordinary chat POST in the same context, this `record_call()` can consume the chat request's leftover wire attempts: `HttpTransport.post()` now always populates `_WIRE`, ordinary chat callers do not consume it, and `post_once()` neither resets nor records it. Consequently, `evaluate_vision_assessment()` can persist a `jev_eval` whose summary says HTTP 200 but whose attempt timeline contains an unrelated chat response and timestamps. This is reproducible with a chat POST returning 401 followed by a successful `evaluate_once()`, which records attempt statuses `[401]`. Give the one-attempt transport path its own fresh collection and record its actual attempt.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: `harness/_http.py` has no shared wire buffer for a strict Jev call to inherit: `post_once` (`:523-545`) emits `provider_http_attempt` rows with `wire_attempt=1, max_wire_attempts=1` under the per-call `request_id` from `current_provider_request()`, and `harness/jev.py:950-955` opens a fresh `provider_request_context(request_id, ...)` with a new `uuid4()` for `evaluate_once`. `record_call` does not exist at this head (`git grep record_call 8fc28a0e -- harness/jev.py` is empty), so a preceding chat POST's attempts cannot be consumed by the strict assessment.

pr_title: docs(intake): file the keyless-vocabulary contract gap (#413)
title: Verify the vocabulary endpoint before recording a contract gap
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the vocabulary endpoint before recording a contract gap**

The cited probe calls `POST /api/driver/step`, not the keyless vocabulary endpoint. At this commit, `harness/server.py:2557-2570` ignores the supplied `action` field and always invokes `adapter.step()`, so `action: vocabulary` still runs the model-backed decision pipeline. Vocabulary retrieval instead uses `GET /api/driver/vocabulary` (`harness/server.py:1888-1889,2528-2531`), whose implementation in `driver_core/server.py:152-153` returns the vocabulary without making a decision. Consequently, the observed refusal does not establish the contract violation recorded here; correct the probe and disposition before adding this as a distinct open defect under #413.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: The false row is withdrawn and the mis-probe is corrected: `evidence/lane-sessions/w2-2026-11-20/filings/413-correction-t14.md` withdraws `driver-vocabulary-keyless-claim-false`, records that `POST /api/driver/step` never reads `action` and returns byte-identical envelopes with and without it, and re-probes the real route. `docs/found-in-use.md` at 8fc28a0e has no `vocab` row (`git show 8fc28a0e:docs/found-in-use.md | grep -i vocab` is empty), and the keyless route it names exists: `harness/server.py:1901` dispatches `GET /api/driver/vocabulary`.

pr_title: #473: record router health and the ordering produced at each rotation
title: Pass the run ledger when assembling the MCP router
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass the run ledger when assembling the MCP router**

For runs served through the native MCP entry point, rotation recording remains disabled: `harness/mcp.py:1832` still calls `composition.router_for(settings)` without the ledger it created immediately above. Consequently, the router receives `trace=None`, and MCP apply/verify operations produce no `router.rotation` evidence even though their other events reach the run ledger. Update that production assembly path as well, or attach the trace centrally when `engine_for` receives the router and ledger.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: `harness/mcp.py:1831-1837` builds `ledger = composition.ledger_for(settings, caller="mcp")` and then calls `composition.router_for(settings)` with no `ledger=`; `harness/session.py:243-245` turns that argument into `trace = DecisionTrace(ledger) if ledger is not None else None`, so the MCP-built router still carries `trace=None` and `harness/router.py:152-153` writes no `router.rotation` row. The serve path does pass it (`harness/session.py:303` `router_for(settings, ledger=ledger)`), so only the MCP assembly is unrecorded.

title: Normalize ledger paths before calling the trace reader
body:

Calling the newly documented `read_rotations("/path/to/ledger.jsonl")` API raises `TraceError("reader needs a ledger or a path")` instead of returning rotation rows. The delegated `read_trace_events` implementation passes strings into `_segment_paths`, which only accepts objects exposing `segment_paths()` or `.path`; the new tests exercise only ledger objects. Normalize path inputs to a supported source representation while preserving archived-segment reading, so callers can actually inspect persisted runs using the advertised path interface.

The archive half of the same sentence is a different defect already filed from row 55 as #762, which owns the retained-segment gap, so this row adds no second sub-issue for it.

pr_title: #476: record each ceiling refusal with the refused call's outcome
title: Distinguish post-dispatch overruns from calls refused before dispatch
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Distinguish post-dispatch overruns from calls refused before dispatch**

When `record_actual` rejects a billed response, `_record_refusal` still writes `outcome="refused"`, which this change defines as the call not having run. These calls have already run: `tests/test_spend.py::test_unreserved_inflight_overspend_documented` exercises this case, and `JevPolicy._account` can even retain the paid result after the accounting rejection. Task-scope checks reached from `record_actual` or `reconcile` have the same problem. Distinguish accounting overruns from pre-dispatch refusals so the new trace does not classify executed, billed calls as calls prevented by the ceiling.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: `harness/spend.py:1103-1104` still calls `_record_refusal(site="record_actual", ...)` when an already-billed response pushes `spent + outstanding + actual` over the ceiling, and `_record_refusal` (`:418`) hardcodes `"outcome": REFUSAL_OUTCOME`, which `:51-53` defines as 'the refused call's outcome: it did not run'. `record_actual` also reaches `_refuse_over_scope` (`:1122-1126`), whose refusal rows carry the same outcome. Executed, billed calls are still classified as refused before dispatch.

pr_title: #476: record each ceiling refusal with the refused call's outcome
title: Include the binding scope's budget in scope-refusal events
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the binding scope's budget in scope-refusal events**

When a task allowance rather than the session ceiling rejects a call, only the scope label reaches `_record_refusal`; its structured envelope always contains the global governor's numbers. For example, a $0.02 reservation rejected by a $0.01 task scope under a $1 session records `requested=0.02`, `phase_ceiling=1.0`, and `phase_remaining=1.0`, with no structured scope allowance or scope balances. Consumers replaying or classifying the refusal therefore see an amount that fits the recorded envelope and must parse the rounded human-readable reason to recover the actual constraint. Include the rejecting target's allowance, spent, and outstanding balances in the event.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: `harness/spend.py:406-411` builds every refusal envelope from `dual_budget_envelope(self.max_cost, self.spent, self.terminal_reserve, ...)` -- the global governor -- and `:436-437` adds only `"scope": str(scope)`. `_refuse_over_scope` (`:453-458`) passes `requested=amount, scope=target.label` and nothing else, so a task-allowance refusal still records the session ceiling and balances with no scope allowance, scope spent or scope outstanding.

pr_title: fix(flush): wire the campaign trace writer at the product entry (#469)
title: Handle trace initialization failures without aborting campaigns
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle trace initialization failures without aborting campaigns**

If the configured trace ledger exists but cannot be read (for example, due to permissions or invalid UTF-8), `AutonomyLedger.__init__` raises from `_load()` before the campaign executes. The exception handling in `DecisionTrace.record()` cannot catch this because the writer has not yet been constructed. This makes previously independent campaign replays fail because an optional, non-audit trace sink is unavailable, contrary to the documented fail-open behavior. Handle initialization failures as well as append failures so an unavailable trace ledger does not prevent the campaign from running.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: `harness/flush_loop.py:665-674` wraps `AutonomyLedger(str(trace_path), caller="flush-campaign")` in `try/except Exception` and returns `None`, with the comment naming exactly the finding's cases (unreadable file, a directory in its place, invalid UTF-8) and stating that `DecisionTrace.record` cannot absorb a failure that precedes the writer. An unavailable trace sink now leaves the campaign running with no trace instead of aborting it.
